While Apple's reimagined personal assistant is undoubtedly the headliner feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate, this year's update packs plenty of other new features and improvements that don't involve Siri AI. Let me highlight a few of my favorite macOS 27 features for you, and be sure to check out my video where I'll demo each one.

App icon overhaul

macOS 27 modifies nearly every built-in app icon to varying degrees, with several — including Siri, Preview, and Chess — receiving complete redesigns. Other app icons like Finder, Photos, and Reminders have also been refreshed to embrace the Liquid Glass design language. In macOS Golden Gate, virtually no app icon is spared, though many of the changes are quite subtle.

If you watch my video below, you'll see a slider comparison showing how each app icon differs between macOS Tahoe and macOS Golden Gate.

Some changes, like the Photos app, I really love. But others, like Finder, I'm not entirely sold on. Let me know what you think of these app icon changes in the comments below.

Video: macOS 27 top features and changes

Comprehensive HDR support

One of the most surprising things about macOS 27 is its extensive HDR support in the operating system's visuals. Icons, toolbars, and other elements in the Liquid Glass design language now feature higher dynamic range support, and users on HDR-capable displays will notice the difference immediately.

To find out which elements have higher dynamic range, you can use macOS's built-in Digital Color Meter tool to see where shadows or highlights get clipped when looking at SDR values. Be sure to watch my video where I'll explore different areas of the OS to demo HDR support.

If you're a Studio Display XDR user, you've surely already noticed these differences, but even if you haven't splurged on Apple's most expensive display, as long as your third-party display supports HDR, you can enjoy these benefits too.

I recently got hands-on with Asus's ProArt QD-OLED 32-inch 4K monitor, and thanks to that panel's technology, the HDR effect throughout the OS really shines. Unlike Apple's first-party displays with Extended Dynamic Range support, you have to go to Settings > Displays and turn on the High Dynamic Range option yourself to enjoy these benefits.

I've recently started using the Dell UltraSharp U3226Q QD-OLED monitor and I'm really loving it — a review video is coming soon. With both of these displays, HDR elements really pop, like the cursor glow in the new Spotlight/Siri AI interface.

Design updates

macOS Golden Gate packs a ton of design updates in response to user criticism of macOS Tahoe. One of my biggest complaints was the inconsistent corner radii on some windows.

Of course, that wasn't the only issue addressed, but it was the most important one to me. Other fixes include: floating sidebars that now return to full-height edge-to-edge sidebars; redesigned toolbars with prominent dividers; and the Liquid Glass effect itself has been improved, including a new slider that lets users choose their preferred balance between transparency and color tuning.

Cleaner menus

Another major user complaint about macOS Tahoe was the clutter piled onto menus. In macOS Tahoe, nearly every menu item came with its own icon, making the whole menu a mess.

If every menu item has an icon, you eventually run out of meaningful icon options while simultaneously making those that do exist far less effective. I'm really glad Apple finally fixed this problem.

iPhone Mirroring

iPhone Mirroring receives three major improvements on macOS 27, making the feature much more useful in Golden Gate.

  • You can now use Control Center within your mirrored iPhone.
  • You can resize the iPhone Mirroring interface to more closely match the aspect ratio of an iPad mini.
  • You can play DRM-protected content from your iPhone on your Mac without seeing a black screen.

Needless to say, iPhone Mirroring becomes way more practical on macOS 27!

9to5Mac's take

While Siri AI has dominated most of the headlines, macOS Golden Gate is far more than just Siri. I've highlighted a few of my favorite new features in this article, but there's plenty more to discover. Be sure to watch my full video to see everything new in one go, and let me know your favorite new feature in the comments below.
